# PR 12955 retrospective

## What worked

Fresh Team 4 coordinator and technical sessions were verified against managed pane identity, native session records and exact model/effort launches. Opus 5.5 High used existing Claude Code authentication; GPT 6 Sol Xhigh used Pi. Legacy directory names were not treated as model evidence. Both reviewers received identical neutral scope and current safety corrections, and neither read peer conclusions before independent finals.

Installed QML metadata exposed the ObjectModel/list mismatch quickly. The independent source assessment and small headless native Quickshell probe converged on one material defect. Real QsMenuOpener objects plus a synthetic SNI made the distinction between missing rows and a wrong property observable without desktop access. Source-gated predicates and explicit child exits made the causal result inspectable. The coordinator checked raw material evidence as well as seals.

## Deviations and remediation

Opus's broad test helper omitted an immediate comparison against declared expected child status. Recording and manually reading status afterward does not satisfy the current fixture gate. This is explicitly a process deviation, not compliant execution. The helper rule was restated to the reviewer and acknowledged in cleanup.md: every case must declare its expected exit, including intentional negative controls, and stop on mismatch. The broad test totals are not public evidence. The public tray-test pass instead uses Sol's separately gated run; the substantive finding uses the native gated probe plus independent API/source evidence. Publication need not be held for this process-only error because the relied-on claims remain independently supported.

The first synthetic no-menu mock used an unavailable dbus.Variant API. Its acknowledgement prerequisite failed and the runner stopped with exit 90. Failed fixture and sealed raw output are preserved; corrected v2 is separate. Neither no-menu result is needed in the public comment.

Claude Code automatically stored two oversized read-only tool outputs in native session tool-results storage. This was transcript storage, not intentionally relocated review artifacts. All authored review fixtures, reports and run bundles remained assignment-owned.

## Limits and restraint

No full Tray.qml, compositor, focus-grab interaction or fractional-scale screenshot was exercised. Mirrored predicates are not a UI end-to-end test. Integer logical pill widths are not a guarantee of whole device-pixel edges at 1.25x. Estimate-label edge cases and hypothetical spontaneous menu reopening were kept out of the public findings. The native relayout counterexample further bounded the latter concern.

No desktop slots, host services, configuration, identity queries or hardware mutation. Every runtime probe used review.py. Cleanup used recorded run receipts/owned PIDs only; private namespace children exited, and private runtime homes disappeared. Both reviewer cleanup records confirm no outstanding resources. Evidence and source checkouts are preserved.

## Carry forward

Use explicit expected-status parameters from the first test helper. Preserve source gates and native model API checks for QML changes. Stop once material questions are answered or bounded by unavailable rendering resources. Keep neutral reviewer reports separate from concise public synthesis. No confirmed Omadev bug or infrastructure feature request arose. HTML was saved without opening, and publication remains the outer assistant's responsibility.
comment:
One tray-menu regression found at `0778d2f5`.

## Ready tray menus cannot open

In [`Tray.qml:130`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0778d2f55bf95cc05ca8d2ffab2574ee258d967a/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Tray.qml#L130) and the new [`onChildrenChanged` handler](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0778d2f55bf95cc05ca8d2ffab2574ee258d967a/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Tray.qml#L515-L523), `QsMenuOpener.children` is an `ObjectModel`, not an array. On Quickshell 0.3.1, `children.length` is `undefined`; the list is `children.values`. Both opening paths therefore leave `trayMenuOpen` false, even after a menu loads.

A headless probe using real `QsMenuOpener` objects and a synthetic tray application reproduced the following with mirrored base/head logic, not the full tray component:

| Menu state | Base open flag | Head open flag | Diagnostic `.values.length` correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| First click, rows not loaded | `true` | `false` | `false` |
| One menu row arrives | `true` | `false` | `true` |
| Dismiss, then click the loaded menu | `true` | `false` | `true` |

**Impact:** Right-click menus become inaccessible, as do left-click menus for tray items marked `onlyMenu`.

**Suggested change:** Use `trayMenuOpener.children.values.length` in `openTrayMenu()` and `children.values.length` in both handler conditions. The diagnostic correction restored opening after row arrival and on a subsequent click in the probe.

**Optional test improvement:** `tray-unready-sni-test.sh` passes on this broken head because it checks for the faulty expression itself. Add a behavioral positive control showing that a nonempty `QsMenuOpener` model opens the menu, alongside the empty-model case.

**Verified by source inspection:** The tooltip bubble now follows its popup dimensions, monitor pill widths are floored to logical pixels, and agent-limit text explicitly says `% used`. Fractional-scale visual rendering was not verified.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Quickshell 0.3.1, a private D-Bus session and synthetic tray application; source inspection and an isolated run of the tray regression test. The native probe mirrored the changed predicates rather than loading the complete `Tray.qml`. No live compositor, focus-grab interaction or 1.25x visual check.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial source inspection, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical reviews, followed by Astra Medium synthesis and verification against the saved source and targeted evidence. A fresh Astra Medium check assessed presentation and disclosures only.
